title: Linear Activation Probe for Jailbreak Detection: Cross-Family Transfer Replication

original_idea.body:
# Activation Probe Cross-Family Transfer

**Problem:** Whether a linear refusal/harm probe transfers across open model families is unverified.

**Direction:** Train a logistic probe on one open model's activations, test zero-shot on a different family at matched layers, measure AUROC drop.

**Why it matters:** Probe portability determines small-actor deployability. Minutes of training.

**Relevant context:** LessWrong Jan 2026; arXiv:2601.04603.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Probe portability determines whether small actors can deploy a leading scalable jailbreak defense.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Logistic-regression probe on extracted activations; minutes of training.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: train probe, test cross-family, measure AUROC drop.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Public hidden states; cross-family transfer is replication labs underreport.

low_compute.reasoning: Activation extraction plus a linear probe; CPU/GPU minutes.

novelty.reasoning: Activation probes exist; cross-family zero-shot transfer measurement may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Probes exist; cross-family transfer angle may be open.
